package_info.package_name: tablediter, request-plus, requestspro, VMConnect, ethter, quantiumbase
package_info.why_malicious: These packages impersonate legitimate Python libraries and contain hidden code that exfiltrates sensitive data to attacker-controlled servers, downloads and executes further payloads, and uses obfuscation and anti-analysis techniques. The campaign is attributed to North Korean state-sponsored actors (Lazarus Group/Labyrinth Chollima).

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: from tablediter.edt import bounding as bounder; bounder.startingbound('C5AB4C83FDE1')
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Imports a malicious function from a secondary module (cookies.py or edt.py) and executes it, triggering data collection and exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unexpected import and execution of code from a non-standard module during package import.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not execute hidden data collection or network code on import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, packages may perform setup or telemetry, but not covert data exfiltration.
key_indicators: Execution of function with obfuscated name

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Spawns a new Python process to execute additional code, likely to evade detection and run malicious payloads in a detached process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Spawning a detached process to run obfuscated code is a common evasion technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal table editing or HTTP libraries do not spawn hidden subprocesses.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare in legitimate packages, except for explicit plugin or extension loading.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Sends collected system and user data to an attacker-controlled C2 server via HTTP POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltration of local data to an external server is a hallmark of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not send local environment data to unknown servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry, but only with user consent and to trusted domains.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Receives a Base64/XOR-obfuscated Python module from the C2, decodes and decrypts it, then executes it dynamically.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamic code execution of remotely supplied, obfuscated payloads is a critical indicator of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should never execute code received from the network.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Very rare; only in controlled plugin systems with strict validation.

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious package, triggering hidden import and execution of the initial malicious function.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial data collection and process spawning

attack_chain.action: Malicious code spawns a detached subprocess to evade detection and run further payloads.
Collected system/user data is sent to the attacker's C2 server via HTTP POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: C2 server responds with next-stage payload

attack_chain.action: Malware receives, decodes, decrypts, and executes a new Python module from the C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of attacker-controlled code and possible further compromise

behavioral_signatures: Detached subprocess creation with obfuscated code
Outbound HTTP POST requests to untrusted domains
Dynamic execution (exec) of network-supplied, obfuscated code
file_indicators: Presence of builder.py with payload decoding routines
Minimal file structure mimicking popular packages
network_indicators: POST requests to attacker-controlled C2 domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that execute code on import, especially those importing from hidden or non-standard modules. Flag packages that spawn detached subprocesses or make outbound HTTP POST requests to unknown domains. Detect dynamic execution (exec) of code received from the network, especially if it is obfuscated (Base64, XOR). Use file integrity monitoring to spot unexpected files (builder.py, cookies.py) and compare package structure/descriptions to known legitimate libraries.
